clues.q: This large cat of the genus Panthera lives in sub-Saharan Africa and India; adult males have a prominent mane
This large Asian cat has orange fur with black, mostly vertical stripes
These African equines have distinctive black-and-white striped coats, with a pattern unique to each individual
Sometimes inaccurately called a bear, this tree-dwelling, plant-eating marsupial is native to Australia
This bear species endemic to China has a white coat with black patches around the eyes, ears, legs and shoulders
The largest bear and land carnivore, this white-furred animal with black skin is native to the Arctic
This large semiaquatic mammal of sub-Saharan Africa gets its name from the Ancient Greek for "river horse"
This spotted feline is the fastest land animal, capable of running 58 to 65 miles per hour
This soft-bodied, eight-limbed mollusc can radically deform its shape to squeeze through small gaps
Reaching about 100 feet long, this baleen whale is the largest animal known to have ever existed
This North American mammal, the largest of the procyonid family, has a grayish coat of dense underfur
This freshwater fish in the carp family Cyprinidae is one of the most popular pets kept in indoor aquariums
These large semiaquatic rodents have chisel-like incisors, webbed back feet and flat, scaly tails
Often shortened to "T. rex," this large theropod dinosaur lived in what is now western North America
These air-breathing arthropods have eight limbs, fangs that can inject venom, and spinnerets that extrude silk
These marsupials, the largest being the red, are native to Australia and New Guinea
These large African hoofed mammals are the tallest living land animals and the largest ruminants on Earth
This common toothed whale of the genus Tursiops inhabits warm and temperate seas worldwide
The largest living land animal, this species native to sub-Saharan Africa has a long trunk, large ears and curved tusks
clues.a: What is the African bush elephant?

clues.q: Members of the order Anura, these are short-bodied, tailless amphibians; rough-skinned ones are often called toads
These large, mostly plant-eating great apes live in the tropical forests of equatorial Africa
Also called the killer whale, this black-and-white toothed whale is the largest member of the oceanic dolphin family
Sometimes called "duck-billed," this egg-laying semiaquatic mammal is endemic to eastern Australia
Also known as the elk, this is the world's tallest and heaviest species of deer, with broad, palmate antlers
This large Arctic marine mammal is the only living species in the family Odobenidae
Also called puma, mountain lion and panther, this big cat is the most widely distributed wild land mammal in the Western Hemisphere
Also known as the prairie wolf, this North American canine is smaller than its close relative, the gray wolf
These highly specialized Old World lizards are best known for their color-shifting camouflage
This domestic hybrid is the offspring of a male donkey and a female horse
These predatory arachnids have grasping pincers and a segmented tail that always ends with a stinger
This big cat is the only living member of the genus Panthera native to the Americas
Closely related to the mako sharks and the porbeagle, this large shark is one of the biggest living fish, though smaller than the whale shark
clues.a: What is the great white shark?

clues.q: Also called caribou, this deer of the Arctic and subarctic is the only representative of the genus Rangifer
These New World mammals with warning coloration can spray a liquid with a strong, unpleasant scent
These large rodents have coats of sharp spines, or quills, made of keratin that protect them from predators
This spiny mammal lives in Europe, Asia and Africa; no living species of it is native to Australia or the Americas
Noted for slow movement, the tree-dwelling species of these mammals hang upside down in Central and South American rainforests
These armored mammals of the Americas are related to anteaters and sloths; some species are told apart by the number of bands
This Late Jurassic plant-eating dinosaur had kite-shaped upright plates along its back and spikes on its tail
Its name means "three-horned face"; this was one of the last non-avian dinosaurs, living until 66 million years ago
Sometimes called "white ants," these wood-eating social insects are actually highly derived cockroaches
Also known as the lesser panda, this small reddish-brown mammal with a ringed tail is native to the eastern Himalayas
This whitish-gray spotted cat has a thick, bushy tail and broad paws adapted to cold, mountainous environments
The largest land-dwelling member of the weasel family, this solitary carnivore has a reputation for ferocity out of proportion to its size
Also called the white fox, polar fox or snow fox, this small canine of the far north has thick fur that camouflages it against snow in winter
This medium-sized, burrowing, nocturnal African mammal is the only living member of the order Tubulidentata
Endemic to a handful of Indonesian islands, this monitor is the largest living species of lizard
Native to every South American country except Chile, this semiaquatic grass-eater is the largest living rodent
This small marine fish of the genus Hippocampus swims with an upright posture and has a curled, grasping tail
These extinct relatives of elephants had spirally twisted tusks; some species were adapted to cold environments
This domesticated South American camelid has been used as a meat and pack animal by Andean cultures since pre-Columbian times
Males of this Arctic toothed whale have a spiraled tusk, actually a protruding left canine, up to about 10 feet long
Sometimes known as sea cows, these large, fully aquatic, mostly plant-eating mammals have paddle-like tails
Also called the suricate, this small mongoose of southern Africa has foreclaws adapted for digging
This mole salamander reaches adulthood without metamorphosis, remaining fully aquatic with obvious external gills
The size of a small dog, this black-furred marsupial became the world's largest carnivorous marsupial after the thylacine died out
These short-legged, muscular marsupials of southern and eastern Australia have small, stubby tails
Also called the forest giraffe, this striped mammal is endemic to the Democratic Republic of the Congo
Also called scaly anteaters, these mammals of the order Pholidota live in Asia and sub-Saharan Africa
This small dromaeosaurid dinosaur lived in Asia about 75 to 71 million years ago; its type species was found in Mongolia
This small carnivorous mammal of the family Herpestidae is native to southern Europe, Africa and Asia
With just four living species, the family of these African carnivores is one of the smallest in the class Mammalia
This wild cat of Africa and Asia has long legs, a sandy or reddish-tan coat and long, tufted ears
This mustelid is also called an ermine, especially in its pure white winter coat once worn by monarchs
Making up most of the world's camels, this tallest camel species has a long curved neck and a single hump
These ancient lobe-finned fish are more closely related to lungfish and tetrapods than to ray-finned fish; one genus, Latimeria, survives
Despite the name, these arthropods of the family Limulidae are not crustaceans but relatives of spiders and scorpions
Also known as the sand puppy, this burrowing rodent is native to the Horn of Africa and parts of Kenya
The smallest fox species, this native of North African deserts has unusually large ears that shed heat
This long-fingered lemur of Madagascar has ever-growing, rodent-like teeth and a special thin middle finger for extracting grubs from tree trunks
This marine mammal is the only living member of its family; its closest modern relative, Steller's sea cow, was hunted to extinction
All living species of these haplorhine primates are native to Maritime Southeast Asia, mainly Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia and the Philippines
About the size of a house cat, this plant-eating, mainly nocturnal Australian macropod is the only member of the genus Setonix
Historically called the pygmy chimpanzee, this is the smallest species of great ape
Sometimes called spiny anteaters, these quill-covered mammals of Australia and New Guinea are, with the platypus, the only living mammals that lay eggs
Also known as the Tasmanian tiger or Tasmanian wolf, this extinct carnivorous marsupial once lived in Australia, Tasmania and New Guinea
Commonly called the saber-toothed tiger, this extinct cat was not closely related to the tiger or other modern cats
Though not an antelope, this mammal of western and central North America is colloquially called the American antelope
Endemic to New Zealand, this lizard-like reptile is the only living member of the order Rhynchocephalia; its Maori name means "peaks on the back"
Native to the Southwestern U.S. and Sonora, Mexico, this heavy, slow-moving reptile is the only venomous lizard native to the United States
This small reddish and gray-brown deer, well adapted to cold, ranges from the Mediterranean to Scandinavia and east to northern Iran
These carnivorous marine crustaceans of the order Stomatopoda, with more than 520 living species, are major predators in shallow tropical waters
Also known as the bearcat, this tree-dwelling viverrid of South and Southeast Asia has popcorn-scented musk glands and a prehensile tail
Also known as the honey bear, this tree-dwelling relative of raccoons and coatis is the only member of the genus Potos
This slender, long-tailed, cat-like carnivore of the family Eupleridae is endemic to Madagascar
This antelope of the Eurasian steppe once ranged across the mammoth steppe from the British Isles to Beringia during the Pleistocene
This large wild goat lives in the mountains where Central and South Asia meet, including the Karakoram and Himalayas
This large ungulate of the goat-antelope subfamily Caprinae lives in the eastern Himalayas; one subspecies is named for Bhutan
These aquatic salamanders of the genus Proteus are the only exclusively cave-dwelling chordates in Europe
Endemic to the eastern and central United States, this aquatic giant salamander is the largest salamander in North America
Also known as the noombat, this daytime-active marsupial eats almost nothing but termites
Endemic to Borneo's mangrove forests, this reddish-brown Old World monkey has an unusually large nose
These amphibious gobies can survive for long periods both in and out of water and move about on land by jumping
These tropical fish are known for "shooting down" insects on land with jets of water spit from their specialized mouths
The third-largest antelope, this forest dweller of sub-Saharan Africa has a reddish-brown coat with white-yellow stripes and spiraled horns
Also called the manul, this small wild cat has long, dense light-gray fur and rounded ears set low on the sides of its head
Also called the mountain devil or moloch, this lizard endemic to Australia is the sole species in its genus
Endemic to the northern Gulf of California, this critically endangered porpoise is the smallest of all living cetaceans
This large South American canine has markings like a red fox's but is neither a fox nor a wolf
Males of this long-snouted, fish-eating crocodilian have a bulb on the snout resembling an earthenware pot called a ghara
